note: Rejudged RFC 4301 Section 7.3: "Also, the receiver MUST discard non-initial fragments that do not comply with the security policy applied to the overall packet." All four existing covers were reread; their tags and claims are unchanged. The two packet covers install the original port-constrained tunnel Child selectors through the production creator, but explicitly opt into fixture-only noninitial-fragment permission before the real backend installs each state. The helper reads both actual installed states, requires permission true and the complete original directional selectors, and separately requires the production childStateScope permission to remain false. This supplies the fragment-admission precondition without claiming bilateral NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO negotiation, which production IKE does not perform. Both cases split the original inner UDP shape and send non-initial before initial, each in its own authenticated ESP packet. The conforming source must reassemble and deliver with XfrmInNoPols unchanged. The outside-source packet must not deliver and must produce exactly one XfrmInStateMismatch with XfrmInNoPols and XfrmInPolBlock unchanged; explicit permission prevents a missing-permission refusal from standing in for that selector check. The boundary positive supplement pins the inbound port selector and transform template; the boundary negative supplement requires malformed selectors to be refused rather than widened and a BYPASS policy to carry no template. The real kernel scope matcher checks the reassembled flow against the receiving state and records StateMismatch on refusal. Retain the existing enforced classification for this whole-packet policy-discard row, with no wider RFC conformance promotion. This is not evidence for the separate unnegotiated-fragment rule RFC4301-7.3-4, IKE negotiation, mixed-protection-context separation or a deliberately broken-kernel discriminator.
